key_insight: DeltaChargeNet predicts charge density from atomic structures, enabling large-scale electronic and quantum transport simulations without the full DFT self-consistency loop.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports simulations of disordered semiconductor devices while preserving electrostatic barriers critical to transport predictions.
method: Train an equivariant graph network to predict density corrections relative to atomic superposition, enforcing charge neutrality.
Apply a secondary ML model to compensate for residual charge-density errors.
Use predicted densities with full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO and non-equilibrium Green’s functions.
evidence_signal: Tests on HgCdTe alloys and Au/HgCdTe/Au devices achieved maximum bulk band-energy errors below 10 meV and layer-resolved potentials within 0.1 eV of self-consistent DFT; transport was demonstrated for an 11,220-atom infrared detector.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested material systems remains unestablished, and both charge neutrality and residual compensation are important for accurate device potentials.
paper_title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
